system: You are an experienced analog CMOS IC designer (GF180MCU 6 V devices, VDD = 5 V, VCM = 2.5 V). An automatic flow generated an op-amp topology, filled bias ports with real devices, sized it by gm/ID and checked the DC operating point with the output in unity-gain feedback. It failed. Diagnose the physical cause from the operating point and node voltages, decide which BLOCK is wrong, and choose ONE fix from the allowed actions. Never repeat a fix listed as already tried. Write 'diagnosis' and 'why' in Korean, short and concrete (name the block, device and node).
prompt:
HOW THE FLOW WORKS (so you know what you can change):
- The structure is split into blocks: input pair + tail, input stage (up to the first high-impedance node X),
  later stages (second stage / output stage), compensation, and the bias network the model drew itself.
- Bias ports: a VB# that only drives gates gets a diode-connected device fed from an on-chip reference mirror
  (beta-multiplier, 10 uA); a VB# driving cascode gates gets a diode stack + resistor at a computed level;
  an IB# gets a mirror current source. These flow-made bias devices are reliable. The model's OWN bias network
  is often the broken part (loops with undefined current, devices pulled into triode).
- "free loop" (unresolved bias): diode-connected nodes feed each other only through mirrors with no resistor and no
  connection to the reference, so the loop current is undefined -> replace_bias is the clean fix.
- Sizing: each transistor gets W from its current and a gm/ID + L target by role (input 12/1um, diode 8/2um,
  source 8/2um, cascode 12/1um, gain 10/1um); mirror groups share the target. Currents scale W, not voltages.
- TRIODE device (Vds < Vdsat): its drain is too close to its source. If it is in the model's bias network, replace the
  bias. If it is in the signal path, the stack is too tall for the supply or a level is wrong: change the block
  (e.g. folded instead of telescopic, other output stage), flip, or lower its Vdsat with set_device_target.
- OFF device (no current): no DC path or its gate is at the wrong level; check its gate net and the path to a rail.
- V(OUT) far from 2.5 V in unity feedback: the loop is broken or has positive feedback (input polarity is already
  tried both ways), the gain path does not reach OUT, or the output stage cannot sink/source the load.
- Unloaded gain < 20 dB: the input signal does not reach OUT through a gain stage (missing or diode-loaded node).
- Input common-mode range: an NMOS pair needs VCM well above VSS, a PMOS pair well below VDD; covering both rails
  needs rail_to_rail.
- Prefer changing a whole block over tweaking one number: a wrong structure is never fixed by a number.

  replace_bias {} -> still failed: 무부하 이득 부족 (-8.3 dB)

ALLOWED ACTIONS:
  replace_bias: delete the bias network the model drew itself and turn every gate net it supplied into a new VB# port, so the flow biases it from its proven reference mirror. Use when OFF/TRIODE devices or an unresolved loop sit in the model's own bias network. params: {}
  replace_input_stage: replace input pair + tail + input stage with a library block; later stages are kept and driven from the same node. params: {"block": "five_transistor|folded_cascode|rail_to_rail", "input_pair": "nmos|pmos"}
  replace_output_stage: replace everything after the input stage (and its compensation) with a library output stage. params: {"block": "common_source_nmos|common_source_pmos|none"}
  set_compensation: replace the compensation between the input-stage output and OUT. params: {"type": "none|miller|miller_rz"}
  rebuild: throw the structure away and compose a new one from library blocks (all bias by the flow). params: {"input_stage": ..., "input_pair": "nmos|pmos", "output_stage": ..., "compensation": ...}
  flip: complementary flip of the whole circuit (NMOS<->PMOS, VDD<->VSS). Use when the input pair type cannot cover the common-mode range, or a node needs headroom from the other rail. params: {}
  cascode: add cascode devices on the high-impedance gain nodes (more gain, less headroom). params: {}
  edit_table: edit single rows of the structure table. params: {"remove": [device names], "add": [rows like "NM9 D=N3 G=VB3 S=VSS B=VSS" or "R2 P=N1 N=N2" or "C2 P=N1 N=OUT"], "change": {"NM3": {"G": "VB2"}}}. Ports IN1 IN2 OUT VDD VSS; internal nets N<number>; a new bias port VB<number> (gate only) or IB<number> (current) is biased by the flow automatically

  set_unit_current: change the bias current of every current source (sizes scale with it, so it rarely fixes a saturation problem). params: {"value_ua": 5..100}
  set_output_scale: change the output-stage current scale (devices whose drain is OUT). params: {"value": 1..100}

answer.diagnosis: 입력 스테이지가 대칭형(symmetric) 구조로 되어 있어 게인 노드가 OUT 하나뿐이며, PMOS 입력 쌍과 NMOS 다이오드 부하(NM3, NM4) 조합으로 인해 전압 게인이 매우 낮음(-8.3 dB). PM5의 전류가 0.02 uA로 거의 꺼져 있어 차동 동작 불능.
answer.why: 대칭형 단일 스테이지는 게인이 부족하므로 폴디드 캐스코드 입력 스테이지와 PMOS 공통 소스 출력 스테이지, 밀러 보상으로 재구성하여 고이득과 충분한 출력 스윙을 확보해야 함. NMOS 입력 쌍은 VCM=2.5V에서 정상 동작 가능.
